pr_title: Set DLL flag on R2R binaries
pr_body:
Always set the IMAGE_FILE_DLL flag on output assemblies with ReadyToRun code even if the corresponding input IL assembly misses it. This is required for R2R relocations to be processed by the OS loader on Windows 7 and Windows 8.1. Fixes #54440. @dotnet/crossgen-contrib

The corresponding code in the old Crossgen: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8a20ae03566e3aabb0c95d2bb206a9ee780db4fd/src/coreclr/zap/zapwriter.cpp#L479-L482
where `m_isDll` is unconditionally set to `true` in `ZapWriter::Initialize`: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8a20ae03566e3aabb0c95d2bb206a9ee780db4fd/src/coreclr/zap/zapwriter.cpp#L51
pr_comments: might be good to run cg2 outerloop pipeline to ensure it doesn't cause any other regressions.
Azure Pipelines successfully started running 1 pipeline(s).
we need to evaluate whether we backport this to preview6. My recommendation is to rel-note unless we feel it affects win8+ (which doesnt appear to be the case)
@mangod9 Has anyone actually tried that scenario on Windows 8.1?
All test failures are known and unrelated.

issue_context.title: R2R causing crashes on Windows 7
issue_context.body:
Machine OS: win7 SP1
Repro steps:
1. Install .NET 6 prevew 6 SDK-6.0.100-preview.6.21315.23(runtime-6.0.0-preview.6.21306.1) from https://github.com/dotnet/installer--Main branch
2. Run "dotnet new console" in CLI .

Expected Result:
Create project successfully

Actual Result:
NET Host stop working.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/65637796/122354245-63628b00-cf83-11eb-8f6d-39cc736cc23d.png)

comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one area label.
@jeffschwMSFT Can you route this to someone who can investigate an SEHException when restoring a newly created project?  The same failure may well happen whenever you try to build a project.

@agocke can you take a look?  Did we take any toolset changes/crt changes?

cc'ing @AaronRobinsonMSFT for visibility (though the sehexception is generally just a generic error)
Huh, haven't taken any specific changes that I know of. I'll take a look.

@agocke I would guess we are using a missing export or missing a native dependency entirely. Having a DMP or a [ProcMon](https://docs.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/procmon) trace of this would help narrow down the issue.

Per Jan,

> It looks like something has overwritten the memory where the target address should have been by these values. These addresses should point to fixup helpers. Looks like something went wrong with applying PE file relocs; or the relocs are not emitted correctly into R2R image.

This does appear to stop crashing when running without R2R.

On my Win7 machine with SDK 6.0.100-preview.6.21321.7 it is crashing with Access violation - code c0000005 on the call below:
```asm
int Microsoft.Build.CommandLine.MSBuildApp.Main(string[])
    push    rbp
    push    rdi
    push    rsi
    push    rbx
    sub     rsp, 56
    lea     rbp, [rsp + 80]
    mov     qword ptr [rbp - 48], rsp
    mov     rsi, rcx
    call    qword ptr [0xa2380]   // Microsoft.Build.CommandLine.MSBuildApp (CCTOR_TRIGGER)
```

Apparently `DIR64` relocations in `MSBuild.dll` are ignored by the OS.  Probably because the file is not marked as a DLL:
```
Dump of file dotnet-sdk-6.0.100-preview.6.21321.7-win-x64\sdk\6.0.100-preview.6.21321.7\MSBuild.dll

PE signature found

File Type: EXECUTABLE IMAGE

FILE HEADER VALUES
            8664 machine (x64)
               3 number of sections
        B7A968BC time date stamp
               0 file pointer to symbol table
               0 number of symbols
              F0 size of optional header
              22 characteristics
                   Executable
                   Application can handle large (>2GB) addresses
```
After I set the `DLL` flag on `MSBuild.dll` and `dotnet.dll`, `dotnet new console` finished successfully.

@dsplaisted @richlander do you feel this requires a backport to preview6? Also @vdanche checking on what Windows versions this is failing on. You do mention it doesnt repro on 10, but how about win8/8.1 etc? 
If its win7 only we will relnote it.

> do you feel this requires a backport to preview6?

No.

Thanks. @vdanche, if this repros on other windows versions please let us know. 

@jeffschwMSFT fyi.
@vdanche confirmed that this repros on 8.1 as well. We will evaluate whether to backport.
Created #54604 in case we decide to fix this in preview6.
Ouch. I'm happy to have others make the call. I still probably wouldn't do it. I suspect that there are very few preview users on Windows 7 and 8.1.
Hi @dsplaisted @marcpopMSFT what are your thoughts on this since this is affecting the sdk in preview6.

From CLI data, win8 and win7 make up .5% of preview usage combined. It'll likely affect a few hundred users in total which isn't great. Worth raising in tactics perhaps as we're still seeing preview 6 fixes come through.
Ok, thanks for the info, since the preview6 PR is ready we will ask for approval.

review_comments: The only bit of `dllCharacteristics` that we used was `AppContainer`, which seems to do nothing for DLLs.  No bits of `imageCharacteristics`, except the default ones, should be set either.
I think this flag does nothing on DLLs.  The C# compiler does not even have an option to set it on a DLL.
but in this case it can also be an exe or since its marked with `IMAGE_FILE_DLL` it does not matter?
We always use a host and never run a R2R binary directly.  In what scenario can it be an .exe?

Since we produce a DLL, it should not be used.  In the past we used to take the image base from the input file, later Tomas changed this code to use a constant, making the condition half-meaningless: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/31663/files#diff-a9a3ebc34e374980992ac65229a97d382e87ba63f7a937b747eca3b51ae6c4ebR582
